ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of side $AC$ of $\triangle ABC$, intersecting $BC$ at point $D$ and intersecting $AC$ at point $E$. If $BC = 8\text{cm}$ and $AD = 5\text{cm}$, what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE$ is the perpendicular bisector of side $AC$ in $\triangle ABC$, and $AD=5\text{cm}$, \\
then $DC=AD=5\text{cm}$, \\
thus $BD=BC-DC=8-5=\boxed{3}\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, B, D, and C are on the same straight-line base, and D is located between B and C; the line DE starting from D intersects side AC at E. Then reason: The problem gives that DE is the perpendicular bisector of AC, therefore point D on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from points A and C, so AD = DC. It is known that AD = 5 cm, so DC = 5 cm. Also because BC = 8 cm, and D is between B and C, therefore BD = BC - DC = 8 - 5 = 3 cm.
